title: Still highly recommend the cast album to anyone who hasn’t listened! ...
transcript: A drastically revised version of one of my favorite Broadway flops is on an international tour that came to New York, so I had to check it out. This is Sting's musical of the Last Ship. He wrote the music, it's inspired by his life, and he's in the cast too, though he doesn't play himself. Also, the reggae musician Shaggy is in the cast in a new role created just for him. And this is my overarching review of the production as someone who loved the original. If people are interested, I might do a part 2 with a more detailed breakdown of the differences, but I have like two full pages of notes on that which I don't have time to include in this video. The reason I have so many thoughts is that despite running on Broadway for only a few months, I managed to see it twice. So I'll admit that I have some bias here, that I'm sentimentally attached to that original version. Even still, though, I feel pretty confident in saying that the revisions have made this show catastrophically worse. Which is really sad, because this has been Sting's passion project for so long, and in his desperation to make it work, he's tinkered with it to death. It feels like something out of a Greek tragedy. Especially because I think I understand what they were going for. I think they were trying to fix what was, to be fair, the biggest problem with the original. which was that the details of the titular Last Ship plotline made no sense. In this version, the labor crisis feels more grounded in reality. The details of what they're facing and how they're trying to protest it, feel clearer, and several of the more featured ensemble characters have been turned into real roles. The goal being, I think, to put more emphasis on the workers and families of this shipbuilding community that Sting is trying to honor by keeping this musical alive. But unfortunately, in trying to give it more logical, real world sense, it has lost all of its dramatic sense. Where there were once plot holes, there are now just awkward, lopsided lumps where they tried to fill them in. The whole show feels like it's just lumbering forward like a car with square wheels and of sagging bumpers scraping the road and constantly sputtering from its exhaust pipe. By contrast, the original was more like a soapbox car. Like, probably not up to code, but it's taking you for a ride. The original relied on well worn cliches, but in those cliches there was a sense of focus, an easy emotional hook to latch onto this earnest story. Both versions indulged in some hyper-sentimentality, but if the original was wearing its heart on its sleeve, this version is kind of kicking its heart around on the dusty floor. Even the music direction feels slower and more laborious. A lot of the added music leans into like loose conversational recitative, which on its own might have been fine, but it ended up contributing to the lethargic and amorphous feel overall. And like I said, I won't get into spoilers or specifics, but there were a couple isolated choices, particularly related to Gideon and Meg, that just absolutely kneecapped it. The plot beats that had me openly weeping in 2014 this time left me completely cold, and for that alone, jail!
